Ecclesiastes 2 · The Vanity of Pleasure and Labor
12C.3 To seek mirth and pleasure is vanity.
13A.2 Every man should enjoy the good of all his labor.

points: Solomon proves himself with mirth and pleasure and finds it also vanity; laughter is madness, and mirth accomplishes nothing.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 2: The Vanity of Pleasure and Labor

points: He gives his heart to wine while still keeping wisdom, and lays hold on folly, trying to see what was good for the sons of men to do under heaven all the days of their life. Solomon is letting us know that he did it all, that he did everything.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 2: The Vanity of Pleasure and Labor

points: Solomon builds houses, plants vineyards, and makes gardens, orchards, and pools of water for irrigation. His kingdom was not a bunch of hard clay houses; he had irrigation systems and everything that grows on a vine.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 2: The Vanity of Pleasure and Labor

points: He gathers servants born in his house, great and small cattle, silver and gold, the peculiar treasure of kings, and men singers and women singers. Solomon had bands, instruments with bands, and musical instruments of all sorts.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 2: The Vanity of Pleasure and Labor

points: Solomon grows greater than all before him in Jerusalem, and out of everything he had, his wisdom still remained with him. He withheld his heart from no joy.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 2: The Vanity of Pleasure and Labor

points: Yet when he looks on all the works his hands had wrought, all is vanity and vexation of spirit, and there is no profit under the sun. With all he had, he still fell victim to the lust of the flesh, and what he did had no purpose.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 2: The Vanity of Pleasure and Labor

points: Solomon turns to behold wisdom, madness, and folly, saying whatever the man coming after the king does has already been done; he already did everything that people want to do.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 2: The Vanity of Pleasure and Labor

points: He sees wisdom excels folly as light excels darkness, yet one event, death, happens to the wise man and the fool alike. Everything the wise man has and everything the fool has, they all go to the same grave.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 2: The Vanity of Pleasure and Labor

points: There is no remembrance of the wise more than the fool forever, and all shall be forgotten; therefore he hates life, for the work under the sun is grievous and all is vanity.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 2: The Vanity of Pleasure and Labor

points: Solomon hates all his labor because he must leave it to the man that comes after him, and Solomon's son was a very dumb young man. All the vineyards, servants, gold, and silver were lost to a foolish person behind him.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 2: The Vanity of Pleasure and Labor

points: No one knows whether the heir will be a wise man or a fool, yet he will rule over all the labor. Everything Solomon worked hard for must be left to somebody coming after him who could lose it all.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 2: The Vanity of Pleasure and Labor

points: This is a great evil: a man labors in wisdom, knowledge, and equity, then leaves it to a man that has not labored for it. His days are sorrows, his travail grief, and his heart takes no rest in the night.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 2: The Vanity of Pleasure and Labor

points: There is nothing better for a man than to eat, drink, and make his soul enjoy good in his labor, for this is from the hand of the Most High. The Most High gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy to the man that is good in his sight.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 2: The Vanity of Pleasure and Labor

points: Solomon is expressing his state of depression and mental well-being: you build up riches all your life but you still die, and your estate goes to somebody else who may be wise or foolish with it.
